If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.

- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.

It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.

- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

- review-triage:review-triage-loop: レビュー・トリアージ・修正の 3 つを上限回数まで繰り返し、収束したか止まったかを人間に返す。各回で review-triage と review-triage-fix を呼び、終了条件に当たったら理由を添えて止める。「レビューから修正までを回して」「収束するまで繰り返して」「review-triage-loop を実行して」のような依頼で使う。引数で上限・レビュースキル・そのオプション・モデル・全量の起点にする派生元のブランチ (--base)・回数の閾値と段の走らせ方 (どちらも review-triage-fix に渡す) を指定でき、省略時は設定の既定に従う。

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. - code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. content.text:
Review target: `bbf28a4..2a84e12`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

283	+

+
+### 全量の起点
+
+**全量の起点は、ブランチの作り始めのコミットで、次の順で決める。**
+
+1. レビュー結果の `scope` が `full` なら、その `base` をそのまま使う。`review-request` が、起点のブランチと HEAD の merge-base (共通祖先のコミット) として求めたものである (正本は [review-request の SKILL.md](../../review-request/SKILL.md) の手順 2)。
+2. 周回の中で呼ばれ、周回が起点のブランチを決めていれば、そのブランチと HEAD の merge-base (`review-triage-loop` は [loop-flow.md](../../review-triage-loop/references/loop-flow.md) の G0 で決めたブランチ、`review-loop` は `loop.yaml` の `review.base`)。
+3. それ以外は、`origin/HEAD` が指すブランチ (`review-request` が引数 `--base` の無いときに使うものと同じ) と HEAD の merge-base。
+
+派生元が別の作業ブランチで、起点を `origin/HEAD` から求めたときは、派生元の作業ブランチの変更もこのブランチの変更として扱われ、(1) が成り立たない行が増える。そうなった指摘は、D8 が無かったときと同じ判定になる — 前からある欠陥を、このブランチの欠陥として判定するだけで、却下が増えることはない。
+
+### (1) 対象の行が変わっていないか
+
+**指摘の対象の行 (`file` と `line`。複数の行にまたがる指摘はそのすべて) が、全量の起点から HEAD までに変わっていないことを確かめる。** 例えば、行ごとに `git blame -L <行>,<行> HEAD -- <ファイル>` でその行を最後に変えたコミットを求め、`git merge-base --is-ancestor <そのコミット> <全量の起点>` が成功すれば、その行はこのブランチのコミットで変わっていない。ファイルがこのブランチで新しく作られたなら、(1) は成り立たない。
+
+### (2) 全量の起点の内容でも同じ欠陥が成り立つか
+
+**全量の起点の内容 (`git show <全量の起点>:<ファイル>`) を読み、指摘の主張が同じく成り立つかを、上の「コードとの照合」と同じ仕方で確かめる。** 指摘が別の箇所との食い違い (文書と実装の不一致など) を主張するなら、相手の箇所も全量の起点の内容で読む。相手の箇所をこのブランチが変えたために食い違いが生じたのなら、ブランチの変更が誤りにしたので、(2) は成り立たない。

findings.short_summary: HEAD が起点そのものだと、新しい欠陥が全件 H7 になる
findings.summary: 全量の起点の手順 3 (`origin/HEAD` と HEAD の merge-base) は、HEAD が既定ブランチの先端のとき起点が HEAD になる。(1) は `git blame ... HEAD` で判定するので、未コミットの変更は見えない。
findings.failure_scenario: `main` 上で、コミット前の作業ツリーの変更に code-review を走らせ、review-triage を呼ぶ。起点は merge-base(origin/HEAD, HEAD) = HEAD (または origin/main) になる。未コミットの新しいコードへの指摘は、行が HEAD で変わっておらず (blame は HEAD の内容を見る)、(2) の起点の内容も HEAD と同じなので、(1)(2) とも成り立ち D8 に当たる。本当は新しい欠陥の指摘が全件 H7 (保留) になり、採択されない。code-review スキルは、レビューがコミットの前に走ることを想定している。

findings.short_summary: 2 度目の S6 の判定が、決定表の報告欄に埋まっている
findings.summary: 「2 度目かどうか」の判定アルゴリズム (連続した k 回の窓・J9 の (a)(b)・採択の file の共通) が、停止ノード S6 の「報告に書くもの」欄に書かれている。図にも J9 のような判定ノードにもない。
findings.failure_scenario: ノードと遷移の正本は図と決定表の判定ノードという規約なので、この判定は図から読めず、検査 (judgment_flow_test.go など) の対象にもならない。「末尾の回より前で終わる連続した k 回」は現在の窓と重なる窓を含むので、k>=2 のとき解釈が割れる。たとえば k=2 で回 3・4 が J9 に該当したとき、回 2・3 の窓を『前の窓』と数えてよいのかが読み取れない。読み方が実行者ごとに違えば、前の 2 つの案を推奨するかが変わる。

findings.short_summary: 集計を持たない方針の直上に、実測の主張を足している
findings.summary: 「発火はまれである」の項目に、記録から得た実測の主張 (「文書への指摘のほとんどが採択になっている」・#92 の実例) を足した。直後の項目は「例の発火数・判定の集計はここに持たない。集計のコピーは置き去りになって実物とずれる。発火の実測は記録の値だけを根拠にする」と書いている。
findings.failure_scenario: 記録が増えると「ほとんどが採択」「さらにまれ」の根拠は変わるが、この文は更新されず実物とずれる。同じ種類の複製は reporting.md の「全量の回で採択が 0 件になった回は無かった」と loop-flow.md の S6 の「2 度再開した後も続いた」にもある。規範文書に #92 の個別の件数を埋めており、直下の方針と矛盾する。「考えられる」という推測も、規範の参照先に残る。

findings.short_summary: D8 が D5 (免除) より先で、免除の指摘が H7 になる
findings.summary: 図は D4 -> D8 -> D5 で、D8 に当たると D5 の免除条項 (A1) を評価せずに H7 (保留) になる。D5 は、検出能力の欠落の指摘を却下させないための節である。
findings.failure_scenario: 指摘「検査の正規表現に検出漏れがある」が、ブランチで変わっていない行を指し、全量の起点でも同じ欠陥が成り立つ。D5 の 2 条件はともに成り立つ (関門が 1 つも無い) ので、本来は A1 (採択) になる。D8 が先にあるので H7 になり、採択されない。免除条項の「最も見逃してはならない」という趣旨と、D8 との優先関係がどの文書にも書かれていない。

findings.short_summary: D8 の「当たる例」が「増分が欠陥を持ち込んだ」と書く
findings.summary: 「当たる例」の本文は「修正が読み手を節 X に導くようになったので、増分が欠陥を持ち込んだ」と書く。D8 の条件は「このブランチより前からある欠陥で、ブランチの変更が誤りにしたのではない」である。
findings.failure_scenario: 例の本文が、欠陥を増分が持ち込んだものと読ませ、D8 の定義 (前からある) と矛盾する。この例を入力に D8 を確かめる実行者は、(2) の「ブランチの変更が誤りにしたのではない」と本文を両立させられず、当たる・当たらないの判断がぶれる。持ち込んだのは欠陥ではなく、欠陥への参照である、と書き分ける必要がある。

findings.short_summary: 全量の回だけの例が、直前の例の回番号と合わない
findings.summary: 新しい例「全量の回だけ: 回 1: 採択 6 → 回 4: 採択 2 → 回 8: 採択 0」は、直前の例 (回 1 全量 採択 6、回 2・3 は増分で 3 回目に収束) と回の並びが続かない。
findings.failure_scenario: 直前の例の記録からは、全量の回は回 1 だけである。続けて読むと、同じ記録のこの行が回 4・回 8 を挙げる理由が分からない。「回 1 → 回 3」の例を写す実行者は、全量の回が 1 つしか無いときに行を書くのか、省くのかが分からない。

findings.short_summary: (1) を blame だけで判定し、移動・改名が考慮されない
findings.summary: (1) は `git blame -L <行>,<行> HEAD -- <ファイル>` の最後に変えたコミットが起点の祖先かどうかだけで決める。ファイルの分割・行の移動・整形のみのコミットは区別されない。
findings.failure_scenario: ブランチが、前からある節を別のファイルへ移しただけ (内容は同じ) のとき、blame の最後のコミットはブランチのコミットなので (1) が成り立たず、D8 に当たらない。前からある欠陥が通常の採択に戻り、D8 が防ぎたかった『参照先を直すと範囲が広がる』が再発する。逆方向の誤判定は無いので重大ではない。

findings.short_summary: HEAD が起点そのものだと、新しい欠陥が全件 H7 になる
findings.summary: 全量の起点の手順 3 (`origin/HEAD` と HEAD の merge-base) は、HEAD が既定ブランチの先端のとき起点が HEAD になる。(1) は `git blame ... HEAD` で判定するので、未コミットの変更は見えない。
findings.failure_scenario: `main` 上で、コミット前の作業ツリーの変更に code-review を走らせ、review-triage を呼ぶ。起点は merge-base(origin/HEAD, HEAD) = HEAD (または origin/main) になる。未コミットの新しいコードへの指摘は、行が HEAD で変わっておらず (blame は HEAD の内容を見る)、(2) の起点の内容も HEAD と同じなので、(1)(2) とも成り立ち D8 に当たる。本当は新しい欠陥の指摘が全件 H7 (保留) になり、採択されない。code-review スキルは、レビューがコミットの前に走ることを想定している。

findings.short_summary: 2 度目の S6 の判定が、決定表の報告欄に埋まっている
findings.summary: 「2 度目かどうか」の判定アルゴリズム (連続した k 回の窓・J9 の (a)(b)・採択の file の共通) が、停止ノード S6 の「報告に書くもの」欄に書かれている。図にも J9 のような判定ノードにもない。
findings.failure_scenario: ノードと遷移の正本は図と決定表の判定ノードという規約なので、この判定は図から読めず、検査 (judgment_flow_test.go など) の対象にもならない。「末尾の回より前で終わる連続した k 回」は現在の窓と重なる窓を含むので、k>=2 のとき解釈が割れる。たとえば k=2 で回 3・4 が J9 に該当したとき、回 2・3 の窓を『前の窓』と数えてよいのかが読み取れない。読み方が実行者ごとに違えば、前の 2 つの案を推奨するかが変わる。

content.text:
Review target: `2a84e12..65067b2`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

  同じ分岐を踏んでいることがある。

## 報告しない条件と residual

報告しない条件 (トリアージで却下される種類):

- 壊れる入力・状態を具体に挙げられない一般的懸念
- 既存の関門 (テスト関数名・検査項目名で挙げられるもの) が顕在化を検出する欠陥
- 対象そのものより大きい防御・再現の仕掛けを要求する指摘
- プロセスの遵守が diff から証明できない、という種類の観察
- 整理・統一の好み (放置して壊れるものが無いもの)。リファクタ提案は 1 件まで、その旨を明記して

上に当たるが捨てるには惜しいものは、findings に入れず、末尾の residual リストに
1 行ずつだけ書く (id 無し・summary のみ)。判断の材料は残すが、指摘としては数えない。

## 出力様式

出力先: `/Users/akima/workspace/claude-plugins/tmp/review-20261004-1837-fix-review-triage-gates-92-94-2-code-review-sonnet.yaml` — **この 1 ファイルだけ。** 名前を変えない。出力先のディレクトリが無ければ作る。コミットしない。

```yaml

model: sonnet
level: "high"
run_id: "20261004-1837-fix-review-triage-gates-92-94-2-code-review-sonnet"
scope: incremental
base: "2a84e12"
head: "65067b2"
date: "2026-10-04"
attrs: {}
findings:
  - id: 1
    file: path/to/file.md
    line: 12
    summary: "1〜2 文の要旨"
    evidence: "検証の前払いの節のとおり"
    attrs:
      severity: P2
      confidence: high
residual: []
```

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `skill` / `model` / `level` / `scope` / `base` / `head` / `date` | 上に埋めた値のまま書く。`level` は指定された effort。`head` は作業開始時の HEAD の短縮 SHA と一致すること |

| `attrs` (トップレベル) | 上に挙げたキー以外に残したい情報 (PR 番号など)。無ければ `{}` |
| `findings[].id` | 1 からの連番 |
| `findings[].file` / `line` | 指摘の位置。`line` は不明なら省略 |
| `findings[].summary` | 1〜2 文の要旨 |
| `findings[].evidence` | 「検証の前払い」の節のとおり |
| `findings[].attrs` | レビューが付けた属性 (`severity` / `confidence` など) をそのまま。無い属性を補完しない |
| `residual` | 「報告しない条件」に当たるが残す 1 行メモの列。無ければ `[]` |

- 指摘が 0 件なら `findings: []` と書く。キーを省かない。件数の集計は書かない (読み手が計算する)。

    (作業ツリーの扱いが「共有」なら、実施後は必ず revert し、作業ツリーが不変であることを確認して報告する。
    「使い捨て」なら revert しなくてよい。どちらも節「作業ツリーの扱い」の規則に従う)
  - 対象箇所の逐語引用 (行番号つき)。矛盾の主張なら、矛盾する 2 箇所の両方を引く
- 「〜の可能性がある」「余地がある」という形の主張には、それを実際に起こす入力・状態を 1 つ添える。
- テスト・検査の不在を主張する指摘 (「この入力のテストが無い」「この分岐が実行されていない」)
  は、その入力を実際に通して報告が出ないことを確かめてから出す。確かめられなければ
  confidence を low にする。テスト関数名の列挙や grep だけで結論しない — 別名のテストが
  同じ分岐を踏んでいることがある。

## 報告しない条件と residual

報告しない条件 (トリアージで却下される種類):

- 壊れる入力・状態を具体に挙げられない一般的懸念
- 既存の関門 (テスト関数名・検査項目名で挙げられるもの) が顕在化を検出する欠陥
- 対象そのものより大きい防御・再現の仕掛けを要求する指摘
- プロセスの遵守が diff から証明できない、という種類の観察
- 整理・統一の好み (放置して壊れるものが無いもの)。リファクタ提案は 1 件まで、その旨を明記して

上に当たるが捨てるには惜しいものは、findings に入れず、末尾の residual リストに
1 行ずつだけ書く (id 無し・summary のみ)。判断の材料は残すが、指摘としては数えない。

Review target: `65067b2..c02a76b`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

findings.short_summary: blame -f のパスは起点のパスと限らず、(2) の git show が失敗する
findings.summary: (2) は blame -f が出す「移す前のパス」で起点の内容を読むと書き、移していない行は指摘の file と同じとする。しかし -f が出すのは、その行を最後に変えたコミットでのパスで、起点でのパスではない。起点より前にそのファイルが改名されていれば、どちらの書き方も起点に無いパスを指す。
findings.failure_scenario: スクラッチのリポジトリで、main が old.md を new.md に改名したコミットの後を起点にする。移していない行を git blame -f -M -C -C -L 2,2 HEAD -- new.md すると old.md が出る。(2) の例どおり git show <起点>:old.md を実行すると fatal: path 'old.md' does not exist で失敗する。(2) は確かめられないときは当たるなので、本来は確かめられる前からある欠陥が H7 になる。移していない行は file と同じ、という文も、この入力では成り立たない。

findings.short_summary: 日本語だけの長い行は、別ファイルへ移すと検出されない
findings.summary: 移動が検出されない行を「英数字の少ない短い行」と書くが、git blame の移動・複製の検出は ASCII の英数字の数で点数をつけるので、長くても日本語だけの行は検出されない。このリポジトリの文書は日本語なので、別のファイルへ移した行を「変わっていない」とする手順は、ほとんどの行で効かない。
findings.failure_scenario: スクラッチのリポジトリで、日本語だけの 60 字ほどの行を a.md から d.md へ移し、git blame -f -M -C -C -- d.md を実行すると、ブランチのコミットが返る (-C -C でも同じ)。実行者は、行が長いので検出されると読み、検出されない理由を探すことになる。英数字を 45 字含む行は検出された。結果は D8 が当たらない保守的な側なので重大ではないが、「短い行」という説明が実際の条件を示していない。

findings.short_summary: 「移す元を変えていなければ -C -C」が再現できない
findings.summary: 「移した先のファイルを作ったコミットが移す元のファイルを変えていないときは -C -C が要る」と書くが、その入力では -C -C でも -C -C -C でも検出されなかった。直前の行の「コマンドの振る舞いは、使い捨てのリポジトリで確かめたものだけを書く」に反する。
findings.failure_scenario: スクラッチのリポジトリ (git 2.50.1) で、a.md の内容を変えずに c.md へ複製するコミットを作り、git blame -f -C -C -C -L 2,2 -- c.md を実行すると、複製のコミットが返り、a.md は出ない (1 行のファイルでも、6 行の複製でも同じ)。-C だけが効いたのは、移す元のファイルを同じコミットで変えた場合 (行を切り取った場合) だった。この文の条件のとおりに -C -C を付けた実行者は、検出されないことを説明できない。

findings.short_summary: 「レビューした内容」の 2 分類に、当てはまらない入力がある
findings.summary: レビューした内容を、結果のファイルなら head のコミットの内容、同じセッションでコミットしていない変更を含めてレビューしたなら作業ツリーの内容、の 2 つだけで決める。同じセッションでコミット済みの範囲だけをレビューした場合と、結果のファイルのレビューが共有の作業ツリーの未コミットの変更を含んでいた場合が、どちらにも当たらない。
findings.failure_scenario: review-triage-loop の sub-agent の経路で、コミット済みの範囲 base..HEAD をレビューし、作業ツリーに別の未コミットの編集が残っている。結果のファイルは無く、コミットしていない変更を含めてレビューしたのでもないので、版を HEAD にするか指定しないかが文からは決まらない。指定しない側を選ぶと、未コミットの編集で行がずれ、別の行を確かめる。

findings.summary: (2) は blame -f が出す「移す前のパス」で起点の内容を読むと書き、移していない行は指摘の file と同じとする。しかし -f が出すのは、その行を最後に変えたコミットでのパスで、起点でのパスではない。起点より前にそのファイルが改名されていれば、どちらの書き方も起点に無いパスを指す。
findings.short_summary: blame -f のパスは起点のパスと限らず、(2) の git show が失敗する
findings.failure_scenario: スクラッチのリポジトリで、main が old.md を new.md に改名したコミットの後を起点にする。移していない行を git blame -f -M -C -C -L 2,2 HEAD -- new.md すると old.md が出る。(2) の例どおり git show <起点>:old.md を実行すると fatal: path 'old.md' does not exist で失敗する。(2) は確かめられないときは当たるなので、本来は確かめられる前からある欠陥が H7 になる。移していない行は file と同じ、という文も、この入力では成り立たない。

findings.summary: 移動が検出されない行を「英数字の少ない短い行」と書くが、git blame の移動・複製の検出は ASCII の英数字の数で点数をつけるので、長くても日本語だけの行は検出されない。このリポジトリの文書は日本語なので、別のファイルへ移した行を「変わっていない」とする手順は、ほとんどの行で効かない。
findings.short_summary: 日本語だけの長い行は、別ファイルへ移すと検出されない
findings.failure_scenario: スクラッチのリポジトリで、日本語だけの 60 字ほどの行を a.md から d.md へ移し、git blame -f -M -C -C -- d.md を実行すると、ブランチのコミットが返る (-C -C でも同じ)。実行者は、行が長いので検出されると読み、検出されない理由を探すことになる。英数字を 45 字含む行は検出された。結果は D8 が当たらない保守的な側なので重大ではないが、「短い行」という説明が実際の条件を示していない。

findings.summary: 「移した先のファイルを作ったコミットが移す元のファイルを変えていないときは -C -C が要る」と書くが、その入力では -C -C でも -C -C -C でも検出されなかった。直前の行の「コマンドの振る舞いは、使い捨てのリポジトリで確かめたものだけを書く」に反する。
findings.short_summary: 「移す元を変えていなければ -C -C」が再現できない
findings.failure_scenario: スクラッチのリポジトリ (git 2.50.1) で、a.md の内容を変えずに c.md へ複製するコミットを作り、git blame -f -C -C -C -L 2,2 -- c.md を実行すると、複製のコミットが返り、a.md は出ない (1 行のファイルでも、6 行の複製でも同じ)。-C だけが効いたのは、移す元のファイルを同じコミットで変えた場合 (行を切り取った場合) だった。この文の条件のとおりに -C -C を付けた実行者は、検出されないことを説明できない。

findings.summary: レビューした内容を、結果のファイルなら head のコミットの内容、同じセッションでコミットしていない変更を含めてレビューしたなら作業ツリーの内容、の 2 つだけで決める。同じセッションでコミット済みの範囲だけをレビューした場合と、結果のファイルのレビューが共有の作業ツリーの未コミットの変更を含んでいた場合が、どちらにも当たらない。
findings.short_summary: 「レビューした内容」の 2 分類に、当てはまらない入力がある
findings.failure_scenario: review-triage-loop の sub-agent の経路で、コミット済みの範囲 base..HEAD をレビューし、作業ツリーに別の未コミットの編集が残っている。結果のファイルは無く、コミットしていない変更を含めてレビューしたのでもないので、版を HEAD にするか指定しないかが文からは決まらない。指定しない側を選ぶと、未コミットの編集で行がずれ、別の行を確かめる。

content.text:
Review target: `c02a76b..4be9b6e`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `4be9b6e..ec39575`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

1. **入力の確認**: 入力の経路は 2 つ — 同じセッションの文脈から受け取るか、**別セッションのレビュー結果を YAML ファイルで受け取る** (依頼の運用と様式の正本は [references/review-request.md](references/review-request.md)。依頼文は [review-request](../review-request/SKILL.md) スキルが生成する)。どのスキルかは記録の `skill` に残�
   - ファイル経由の場合、読むのは**依頼文に埋め込んだ出力先の 1 ファイル** (`tmp/review-<識別子>.yaml`)。`head` が現在の HEAD と一致することを確かめてから判定に進む。`residual` の列は指摘として数えず、目を通して気になるものだけ記録の `notes` に写す。**直したい residual は `notes` ではなく、自己採択の指摘 (`orig
   - **出力先には過去の回のファイルが残る。** 識別子で名前が区別できる (成分の正本は [review-request](../review-request/SKILL.md) の手順 3) が、それでも `head` が現在の HEAD と一致するものだけを対象にし、一致するものが無ければ指摘が無い場合と同じ扱いにする — 古い結果を現在の HEAD への指摘として判定すると、
   - **上流が報告のみで走ったかを確かめる** (実行前後で HEAD と作業ツリーが不変)。適用済みなら判定に進まず、その旨を報告して次から報告のみで走らせるよう案内する。
   - 指摘が見当たらなければ、レビューを先に走らせるよう案内して終了する。**勝手にレビューを走らせない。**
2. **設定の読み込み**: `.claude/review-triage.yaml` を読む。読み込みは 3 値 ([references/config-schema.md](references/config-schema.md)) — 「読めない」なら判定を始めずにエラーを報告する。無ければ `--gen-config` を案内して終了する。
   - あわせて `.claude/akm-claude-plugins/review-triage/config.json` を読む ([references/project-config.md](references/project-config.md))。記録の置き場・関門の一覧・検査コマンドを決める。**無くても判定は進むが、関門の一覧が無いと免除条項は使えない** (突き合わせ先が無いまま関門名を書かせると、実在しない名前が検査されない�
3. **判定**: 指摘ごとに [references/judgment-flow.md](references/judgment-flow.md) の図に従って決着させる。
   - 帰結の 4 項目 (D3 で書くもの) は**全件に書く** — D1・D2 で決着した指摘にも記録の材料として残す。
   - 評価 (E1・E2) の結果は、判定がどこで決まっても**すべて記録に載せる** (評価と判定の分離)。照合の仕方は [references/premise-check.md](references/premise-check.md)、ゲートの定義は [references/rejection-gates.md](references/rejection-gates.md)。
   - 境目が判断しづらいときは [references/gate-examples.md](references/gate-examples.md) の対になった例と突き合わせる。
4. **記録の追記**: 記録 YAML に 1 回分を追記する (様式・スキーマの正本は [references/record-schema.md](references/record-schema.md))。`model`・`scope`・`head` を必ず書く。`verdict_reason` には決着ノードの ID を書く。既定の置き場を使うとき、置き場が `git check-ignore` で無視されていなければ、記録を書かずに「`.gitignore` に `tmp/` を�
5. **サマリの再生成と検査**: [記録 README の「書いた後にすること」](references/record-schema.md#書いた後にすること) の 1 と 2 を行う (コマンドと、未設定のときの扱いの正本は [references/project-config.md](references/project-config.md))。
6. **コミット**: 同じ節の 3 のとおり、置き場が git の追跡内 (`git check-ignore` で無視されない) のときだけコミットする — 既定の `tmp/review-triages/` は追跡外なのでコミットしない (判定の仕方・要否・分け方の正本は [記録 README のコミット節](references/record-schema.md#コミット))。**修正はコミットしない** (判断までが�
7. **報告**: 全件数・採択・保留・却下と、決着ノード別の内訳 (生成サマリの推移の表と同じ値) を出す。保留があれば [references/hold-presentation.md](references/hold-presentation.md) の形で提示する。採択があれば [review-triage-fix](../review-triage-fix/SKILL.md) を案内する。**勝手に呼ばない** — 直すかどうかは人間が決める。

content.text:
Review target: `ec39575..d69e724`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `d69e724..13ddb43`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `13ddb43..efb63b9`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/akima/.claude/plugins/cache/akm-claude-plugins/review-triage/0.20.0/skills/review-request

# review-request: レビューの依頼文の生成

別セッションで走らせる上流レビューの依頼文を、雛形 ([review-request-template.md](../review-triage/references/review-request-template.md)) を埋めてファイルに書き出す。**成果物は依頼文のファイル 1 つで、レビューは走らせない。** 走らせるのは人間で、新しいセッションに依頼文のパスを渡す。結果を受け取って判定するのは [review-triage](../review-triage/SKILL.md)。

依頼の運用 (なぜファイルに書き出すか・範囲の規則・各節の理由) の正本は [review-request.md](../review-triage/references/review-request.md) — ここでは言い直さない。

## 引数

```
review-request [<スキル名>] [<モデル名>] [<effort>] [--dir <ディレクトリ>] [--full-review] [--base <ブランチ>]
```

| 引数 | 意味 | 省略時 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<スキル名>` | 依頼文でレビュアに呼ばせるレビュースキル | 手順 1 |
| `<モデル名>` | レビューを実行するモデル | 手順 1 |
| `<effort>` | レビュースキルに渡す effort | 手順 1 |
| `--dir <ディレクトリ>` | 依頼文と結果の置き場。相対パスはリポジトリのルート (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) を基準に解決する。作業ツリーの外は受け付けない (git に無視されていることを確かめられないため) | `tmp/` |
| `--full-review` | 記録に回があっても、範囲を全量 (scope `full`) にする。要否に関わらず全量にする明示の指定 (要否の規則の正本は [review-request.md](../review-triage/references/review-request.md) の「収束後の全量レビューと、その要否」) | 範囲は手順 2 のとおり (記録に回が無ければ全量、あれば増分) |
| `--base <ブランチ>` | 全量の起点を求める派生元のブランチ (別の作業ブランチから派生したブランチなら、その作業ブランチ)。増分の回では使わない | `origin/HEAD` が指すブランチ (手順 2) |

位置引数はこの順で読む。`--dir`・`--full-review`・`--base` は位置引数の前後どちらに置いてもよい。`--full-review` と `--base` は設定のキーを持たない — どちらもブランチや周回ごとに変わる値である。周回の置き場に依頼文を書くスキル (`review-loop`) が、`--dir` を毎回、`--base` と `--full-review` を全量の回に使う。

## 前提知識

- **依頼文を会話に貼らない。** 貼り方が回ごとに変わると、出力先の名前・様式・読み取り専用の条件も回ごとに変わる (理由と実測は [review-request.md](../review-triage/references/review-request.md))。出力先のパスは生成の時点で依頼文に埋め込まれるので、レビュアがそこをずらす余地が無い。
- **雛形の各節 (作業ツリーの扱い・検証の前払い・報告しない条件・出力様式) はそのまま写す。** 生成のたびに言い直さない — 言い直すと、貼り方が回ごとに変わる元の問題に戻る。
- **スキル名とモデル名は推測しない。** 記録の `skill` / `model` にそのまま入るので、依頼したものと違う値が記録に残ると、粒度の比較が狂う。

## 手順

1. **引数と設定を読む**: 引数はスキル名・モデル名・effort と置き場 (様式は上の「引数」)。**スキル名の省略時は `code-review`。モデル名は、引数に無ければ設定 (`.claude/akm-claude-plugins/review-triage/config.json`) の `loop.review_model` を使い、それも未設定なら人間に尋ねる。effort は、引数に無ければ設定の `loop.review_args`、それも未設定なら既定 (正本は [review-invocation.md](../review-triage-loop/references/review-invocation.md) の「effort の既定」)。`ce-code-review` のように effort を受け取らない skill では空にする** (設定のキーの正本は [project-config.md](../review-triage/references/project-config.md))。あわせて設定の `record_dir` を読む (未設定なら既定の `tmp/review-triages/`)。
2. **回と範囲を決める**: 現在のブランチの記録 (`<record_dir>/<ブランチ名>.yaml`。ブランチ名の `/` は `-` に置き換える) を読み、`runs` の数 + 1 を回とする (記録が無ければ 1)。**記録があるのに読めない (YAML として壊れている・`runs` が無い) なら、生成せずにその旨を報告して終了する** — 「読めない」を「無い」に寄せると回が 1 に戻り、過去の回と同じ番号の依頼文ができる。
   - **記録に回が無いか、引数 `--full-review` があれば、scope は `full`。** `base` は、起点のブランチと HEAD の merge-base (共通祖先のコミット) の短縮 SHA (`git merge-base <ブランチ> HEAD` の結果を `git rev-parse --short` で縮めたもの)。起点のブランチは、引数 `--base` があればそれ、無ければ `origin/HEAD` が指すブランチ (`git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` の結果。`origin/main` のような形のまま使う)。起点を分岐元の `main` に決め打ちしないのは、別の作業ブランチから派生したブランチで、派生元のコミットまで範囲に入るため。**`--base` のブランチが解決できない (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet "<ブランチ>^{commit}"` が失敗する)、`--base` が無くて `origin/HEAD` が無い、または merge-base が求まらない (共通祖先が無い) なら、生成せずにその旨を報告し、起点のブランチを人間に尋ねる** — 起点を推測すると、範囲が広すぎるか狭すぎる依頼文ができ、どちらもレビューの結果からは気づけない。
     - 補足は、記録に回が無く `--full-review` も無ければ「ブランチの全量 (起点: `<ブランチ>` との merge-base)」。`--full-review` があれば「ブランチの全量 (`--full-review` による指定。起点: `<ブランチ>` との merge-base)。増分の外を報告しない規則はこの回には当てはまらない」。書き分けるのは、記録に回がある状態の全量の回で、レビュアが前の回の依頼文にあった増分の規則をこの回に当てはめないようにするため。
   - **それ以外 (記録に回があり、`--full-review` が無い) なら、scope は `incremental`、`base` は直前の回の `head`。** `--base` は使わない (あっても無視し、報告にその旨を書く)。補足は「前回の HEAD `<sha>` からの増分。増分の外は、増分が壊した場合のみ報告する」。
   - **置き場 (`--dir`。省略時は `tmp/`) が `git check-ignore -q <置き場>` で無視されていなければ生成せず、「`.gitignore` に置き場 (既定なら `tmp/`) を足してコミットしてから再実行する」と案内して終了する** — スキルは `.gitignore` を変えない。依頼文と結果は設定の `record_dir` に関わらず置き場に置くので、記録の置き場と違って「既定の置き場を使うとき」に限らず常に確かめる (前提の正本は [record-schema.md](../review-triage/references/record-schema.md) の冒頭)。`git check-ignore` は存在しないパスにも効くので、置き場を作る前に確かめる。
   - `head` は現在の HEAD の短縮 SHA。**作業ツリーが clean でなければ生成せず、その旨を報告する** — 依頼文は作業ツリーの扱いを「共有」(依頼した側と同じ作業ツリーでレビューする) で書くので、レビュアは HEAD と作業ツリーが不変であることを確かめて報告する。汚れたまま渡すと、その確認が成り立たない。周回 (`review-loop`) で「使い捨て」に書き換えた依頼文でも、依頼した側の作業ツリーは確かめる (確かめるのはワーカーで、正本は [review-loop の worker.md](../review-loop/references/worker.md) の「回の処理」の手順 4)。
3. **識別子と出力先を決める**: 識別子は `<YYYYMMDD>-<hhmm>-<ブランチ名>-<回>-<スキル名>-<モデル名>`。依頼文は `<置き場>/review-request-<識別子>.md`、レビュー結果の出力先は `<置き場>/review-<識別子>.yaml` (置き場の既定は `tmp/`)。成分ごとの扱いは下の表が正本で、**成分を足す・外す・変えるときは、その行の全欄を確かめる** — 欄を 1 つ書き残すと、その扱いの欠けは次のレビューまで気づかれない (実測: 成分を変えるたびに、外した成分の役割・足した成分の整え方・参照先の規則、と別の欄で 3 回続いた)。識別子はファイル名に使うので、整え方はファイル名に使える形にするためのもの。識別子の衝突 (同じ名前の依頼文か結果が既にある状態) は 1 つずつやり直せるので、厳密な一意性は求めない。

   | 成分 | 出所 | 整え方 | 欠損時の扱い | なぜ入れるか |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | 日時 (`YYYYMMDD-hhmm`) | 生成した日時 | 数字だけなのでそのまま | — (必ず取れる) | 先頭に置くと一覧が時系列に並ぶ |
   | ブランチ名 | 現在のブランチ | `/` と、ファイル名に使えない文字を `-` に置き換える (記録の YAML のファイル名の規則とは別に定める。参照しない) | detached HEAD なら `detached-<短縮 SHA>` | `tmp/` は手元にしか無く、同じリポジトリの別のブランチで同じ回を回すと衝突する (実測) |
   | 回 | 手順 2 | 数字だけなのでそのまま | 記録が無ければ 1。記録があるのに読めなければ生成せず報告して終了 (手順 2) | 同じブランチの過去の回と区別する |
   | スキル名・モデル名 | 手順 1 | `/` と、ファイル名に使えない文字を `-` に置き換える (設定や引数の綴りをそのまま入れない) | 未指定なら手順 1 の既定か人間に尋ねる | 同じ回に複数のレビュアを走らせたとき (同じ分に作れば日時は同じ) を分け、依頼文を開かずにどのレビュアの結果かが分かる |

   - **どちらかが既に存在すれば上書きせず、その旨を報告して終了する。** 同じ識別子で作り直したいときは人間が消す。
4. **雛形を埋めて書き出す**: 雛形の `{{…}}` を次で埋める — `repo` (`git remote get-url origin`)・`repo_dir` (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`)・`branch` (現在のブランチ名)・`base` / `head` / `scope` / `scope_note` (手順 2)・`skill` / `model` / `effort` (手順 1)・`date` (生成日 `YYYY-MM-DD`)・`run_id` (手順 3 の識別子)・`output_path` (手順 3 の出力先を `repo_dir` 起点の絶対パスにしたもの)。置き場が無ければ作る (無視されていることは手順 2 で確かめ済み)。
   - **出力先は絶対パスで埋める。** 相対パスはレビュアの側の cwd (作業ディレクトリ) で解決され、別の場所に書かれた実測がある。
   - **雛形の「対象」の節にある作業ツリーの扱いの行 (`- 作業ツリーの扱い: 共有`) は書き換えず、値「共有」のまま書く** — 「使い捨て」への書き換えは周回 (`review-loop`) のワーカーが行う (正本は [review-loop の worker.md](../review-loop/references/worker.md) の「回の処理」の手順 8)。
   - **依頼文は、同じ置き場の一時名 `.review-request-<識別子>.md.tmp` に書き、埋め残した `{{…}}` が無いことを確かめてから、`mv` で `review-request-<識別子>.md` に改名する。** 置き場を定期的に確かめる側 (`review-loop` のワーカー) は一時名 (`.` で始まる名前) を読まないので、書きかけの依頼文を処理しない。
5. **報告する**: 依頼文のパスと出力先のパス、埋めた値 (対象・範囲・スキル名・モデル名・effort) を出す。**scope が `full` なら、起点のブランチ名と merge-base の SHA、ブランチの出所 (`--base` か、`origin/HEAD` による既定か)、`--full-review` の有無も出す** — 起点を推測しない規則を、人間が報告で確かめられるようにするため。**新しいセッションへ渡すのは依頼文のパス 1 つ**であること、結果が返ったら `review-triage` に出力先のパスを渡すことを案内する。

## 原則

- **レビューを走らせない。** 走らせるかどうか、どのセッションで走らせるかは人間が決める。
- **既存の依頼文・結果を上書きしない。** 回の途中で作り直すと、どの結果がどの依頼に対応するかが辿れなくなる。
- **依頼文のファイルはコミットしない。** 置き場に置き、記録と同じく git の追跡外にする (無視されていなければ手順 2 で止まる)。

## このスキルがしないこと

- **レビュー結果の様式の検査** — 受け取る側 (`review-triage` の手順 1) が担う。
- **依頼文の文面の設計** — 雛形が正本。文面を変えたいときは雛形を直す。
